source: MASQ's material table: price, CO2e per kg of filament at one boundary (filament at the gate; where only the resin was measured, one 1.5 kg CO2e/kg extrusion-and-spool adder, the gap Prusament measured between resin and filament), datasheet strength, wear lines, and the printers' power, bed and purge
co2eBoundary: cradle to gate, kg CO2e per kg of filament; lo and hi are the spread of the cited figures brought to the same gate, mid is the card's number
electricitySource: grid average; a 3 h PLA mask on the X1C is ~0.2 kWh, ~0.07 kg CO2e, https://forum.bambulab.com/t/power-consumption-data/4180

pla.name: PLA
pla.wear: PLA: stiff, the cheapest, the easiest; brittle at a thin rim and it creeps in a hot car (HDT 57 °C); sweat sits in the layer lines; sands and fills well; do not wash hot. The default.

petg.name: PETG
petg.wear: PETG: tougher than PLA and stands 70 °C; strings and is hard to sand; the weakest across layers of the rigid ones (Z 69%): a chin-standing PETG mask flexed on cracks along a layer.

abs.name: ABS
abs.wear: ABS: warps on the big flat contact a face-down print makes (a heated chamber helps, the Kobra has one, the P1S/X1C are passive); acetone-vapour smooths to a gloss; off-gasses styrene while printing and is one the wearables guide says to avoid against skin; ASA is the stronger of the two.

asa.name: ASA

co2eKgPerKg.cited: as ABS: 3.1 virgin resin + 1.5 extrusion and spool

asa.wear: ASA: warps on the big flat contact a face-down print makes (a heated chamber helps, the Kobra has one, the P1S/X1C are passive); holds up in sun; off-gasses styrene while printing and is one the wearables guide says to avoid against skin; the stronger of ABS and ASA and the one to pick of the two.

tpu95a.name: TPU 95A
tpu95a.wear: TPU 95A: flexes to a face, the one material where fit follows the wearer; no supports it will not tear off; slow (43 mm/s at the cap, a night's print); Bambu's datasheet gives a 70° overhang and 20 mm bridge; skin-safe by the datasheet and the guide; cannot be sanded; the mask's rigid-interference lesson does not apply to it.

pa6cf.name: PA6-CF
pa6cf.wear: PA (nylon, CF): the strongest in plane and the weakest across (Z 47%); absorbs water and must be dried; abrasive to brass; expensive; a mask rarely needs it.

pc.name: PC

co2eKgPerKg.cited: 4.7 median, 5.4 mean resin + 1.5 extrusion and spool

pc.wear: PC: the stiffest and the hottest (HDT 112 °C); warps and needs the chamber and glue; overkill for a mask, listed because a helmet-grade shell asks for it.

skinSources: Bambu's datasheets: Skin Hazards: No hazard, every one

sources: https://forum.bambulab.com/t/power-consumption-data/4180 (60-80 W printing, up to 400 W heating)

prusa_xl.name: Prusa XL (2 heads)
prusa_xl.note: slicing profile: the default printer's (vendor/print/printers.json has no Prusa XL row); a PrusaSlicer 3mf reads the same geometry and offers its own printer. Two toolheads: the door to two-material masks.
